terms.definition: A long, whip-like structure a cell uses to swim or move through fluid.
Structures inside a cell that convert nutrients into usable energy (ATP) — often called the cell's 'power plants.'
The compartment inside a cell that stores its DNA (genetic instructions).
A cap of enzymes on the front of the sperm's head that helps it break through the outer coating of an egg cell.
Having exactly half the normal number of chromosomes — true of sperm and egg cells so that when they combine, the full number is restored.
The moment a sperm cell and an egg cell join together to form a single new cell.
The biological process that produces sperm cells in the testes.
